sentences.text: CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA

ORAL ORDER Petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 are before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.2109/2023, pending before the VIII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City,
for the offences punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

entities.text: VIII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 in unison submit that the parties to the lis were before the concerned family Court in M.C.No.837/2026 and have settled their matrimonial dispute amicably by drawing up certain terms and conditions before the mediation center.
The parties as obtained decree of divorce on mutual consent and have parted their ways.
Therefore, they are before this Court seeking quashment of the proceedings.
The parties have appended a copy of the memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of the CPC r/w. Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005 to the petition.
NC: 2026:KHC:13418 HC-KAR 3.

The memorandum of settlement reads as follows:
"5. The 1st petitioner/father undertakes to take care of the minor child's health,
education and maintenance by making payment of Rs.11,00,000/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Only) out of which Rs.10,00,000/- by way of D.D. drawn on Kotak Mahindra Bank, 7th Block, Jayanagar Branch dated 10.02.2026 bearing D.D. No.998010, in favour of minor daughter's mother's i.e. 2nd petitioner's name and Rs.1,00,000/- by way of Cash will be paid at the time of reporting settlement before the Hon'ble Court and the marriage of the daughter will be celebrated by sharing expenses equally.
6. The First Petitioner has already paid the said amount to the Second Petitioner is a sum of 10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs only) at the time of filing the above divorce petition by way of Demand Draft bearing No.998008 dated 05-02-2026, which amount represents full and final settlement towards the livelihood and maintenance of the Second Petitioner and also full and final permanent alimony.
Thus, a total sum of Rs.21,00,000/- is paid to the 2nd petitioner and the 2nd petitioner hereby accept and acknowledge the receipt of the same.

7. That in view of settlement and filing of the above Petition, the Petitioner No.2 has agreed to withdraw the case filed by her under D.V.Act in C.Mis No.140/2022 pending before the Hon'ble IV MMTC Court, Bengaluru.

Similarly, the Petitioner No.2 also agreed to co-operate or consent to close/quashing of the case in C.C.No.2109/2023 pending before the VIII A.C.M.M. Court, Bengaluru, which has Sri Gopal C vs State Of Karnataka on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64386165/
3 been filed by her against the 1st petitioner and his family members.

sentences.text: Further, the Petitioner No.2 has agreed to withdraw the case M.C.No.6341/2022 filed by her for restitution of conjugal rights pending before the Hon'ble V NC: 2026:KHC:13418 HC-KAR Additional Prl. Family Court, at Bengaluru.

entities.text: V NC: 2026:KHC:13418 HC-KAR Additional Prl. Family Court, at Bengaluru
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Likewise, the Petitioner No.1 has agreed to withdraw the case of M.C.No.4866/2022 filed by him for the Relief of declaration pending before the V Additional Prl. Family Court, Bengaluru.

entities.text: V Additional Prl. Family Court, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Both the petitioners state that the above withdrawal of cases is being done voluntarily, without any coercion, compulsion, or undue influence, and entirely out of their own free will and mutual understanding."

In the light of the fact that the parties have arrived at settlement and since it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to accept the application, memo and the affidavit and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.
4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The writ petition is disposed.
(ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.2109/2023, pending before the VIII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, stand quashed.
